text:
julia: quick sanity check — i'm building a compact compatibility matrix to drive router decisions for graceful handoffs across tiers/regions. spotted three recurring gotchas: tokenizer variant mismatch, context-length truncation, and missing tool-calling hooks on some quantized variants. open to suggested columns and thresholds.

mike: +1. maybe we should treat 'tool_call' as a hard requirement for routes that expose tools. otherwise fallback is useless.

devin: Can you list the offending variants? I can run the parity tests.

julia: short list from today's smoke runs:
- region-eu: model-v2-quant lacks tool_call endpoints (returns 501).
- region-us-east: model-v1-legacy uses bpe-v1 tokenizer, while newer variants expect bpe-v2 -> subtle token shifts.
- region-apac: model-v3-8k advertises 8k ctx but runtime truncates at 4k under some mem configs.

sara: ugh. tokenizer mismatches cause eval drift more than latency. we should flag any tokenization delta > 0.5% on our regression tests. :thinking_face:

mike: agree. propose adding capability flags to the model manifest and have the router consult those before deciding fallbacks. e.g. manifest snippet:
```yaml
capabilities:
  tokenizer: bpe-v2
  max_context_tokens: 8192
  tool_call: true
  kv_cache_compatible: false
```

devin: router change sounds reasonable. i worry about churn — models often advertise capabilities but implementations vary. need a runtime verification step when model is onboarded (small parity suite).

julia: that's my thought too — two layers: declared capabilities + runtime parity verification. if parity fails, mark variant as "best-effort" and lower its fallback priority.

infra-bot: ci:parity-checks queued for model-v2-quant in region-eu (job 4921).

mike: routing policy example (pseudocode):
```json
{
  "route_priority": ["variantA", "variantB", "variantC"],
  "fallback_policy": [
    {"condition": "tool_call_required && variant.supports.tool_call == false", "action": "skip"},
    {"condition": "tokenizer_mismatch > 0.001", "action": "demote_priority"},
    {"condition": "runtime_ctx < requested_ctx", "action": "truncate_or_fail"}
  ]
}
```

sara: can we add an explicit quota/latency tradeoff column? e.g. if fallback picks a cheaper variant with 2x latency, console should show estimated latency and billing delta. PMs ask for that often.

julia: yes — UX ask: in rollouts canary UI, show a "fallback exposure" metric: % requests that hit a non-preferred variant + top reasons (tool_call_missing, tokenizer_shift, ctx_truncated).

ui-bot: mock: https://redwood-internal/prototypes/hand-off-metrics (uploaded).

devin: telemetry note — we need these metrics exported per (route, customer_tier, region):
- fallback_rate
- fallback_reason_counts
- tokenization_delta_pct
- avg_truncation_tokens
- fallback_latency_overhead

mike: add alerting: when fallback_rate_by_tier > 3% for > 5m -> page SRE. for premium customers treat threshold as 0.5%.

sara: also add an ingestion tag so console can show per-customer attribution. customers will want to know if their requests were affected.

julia: operational checklist proposal:
1) add capability fields to manifest + update onboarding docs.
2) run runtime parity suite for every new model/variant/region before enabling in router.
3) surface fallback metrics in console (canary and live routes).
4) add alerting thresholds per-tier.
5) create an A/B rollout guard that blocks canary if tokenization_delta_pct > 0.2% or fallback_rate > X.

devin: i'll own the parity suite. i'll add tokenizer and tool-call smoke tests, plus a small ctx-length end-to-end.

mike: i'll prototype router checks and tie into model capabilities API.

sara: i'll own console visuals and the per-route billing delta calc.

julia: thanks — next steps: devin pls add a short spec to the infra repo with exact test vectors, mike pls post a sketch of how router queries model capabilities (api + cache TTL), sara pls drop a mock gif in the prototype link. sync tomorrow 10am. :calendar:

infra-bot: ci:parity-checks started (job 4921).

mike: one more operational edge-case — what if the preferred variant supports tool_call but the fallback advertises tool_call:true but actually throws on attach? runtime check should be to call the actual tool handshake, not just presence of endpoint.

devin: yep — test should include a tool-handshake endpoint call with a lightweight payload. mark variant unhealthy if response != 200 within 500ms.

sara: and UI should display last-known parity timestamp so PMs can see staleness.

julia: perfect. i'll update the roadmap ticket and add these action owners. thanks all. :rocket:
